title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 78 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 465–467 (Night 78, continuing directly from nights-77), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 78 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Ḍawʾ al-Makān, now sultan, is met by the armies of Baghdad and Khurasan under the vizier Dandān, who file past him ten by ten and swear loyalty. He keeps the army in camp ten days, and has Dandān tell the story of his father's death, with his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān listening behind a curtain; the vizier begins with the old devout woman who came to King ʿUmar with five learned slave-girls. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّامِنَةُ وَالسَّبْعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thāminatu wa-al-sabʿūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the eighth and the seventy,
sentences.i: And when it was the seventy-eighth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ الْحَاجِبَ لَمَّا أَمَرَ الْفَرَّاشِينَ أَنْ يَنْصِبُوا خَيْمَةً وَاسِعَةً لِاجْتِمَاعِ النَّاسِ عِنْدَ الْمَلِكِ نَصَبُوا خَيْمَةً عَظِيمَةً عَلَى عَادَةِ الْمُلُوكِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīda anna al-ḥājiba lammā amara al-farrāshīna an yanṣibū khaymatan wāsiʿatan li-ijtimāʿi al-nāsi ʿinda al-maliki naṣabū khaymatan ʿaẓīmatan ʿalā ʿādati al-mulūki
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the chamberlain, when he had commanded the tent-pitchers to pitch a wide tent for the gathering of the people with the king, pitched a great tent according to the custom of the kings.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the chamberlain commanded the tent-pitchers to set up a spacious tent where the people could gather before the king, and they pitched a great tent in the manner of kings.
sentences.n: The print runs أن into the word before it (السعيدان, “the happy — that”); it is read as two words.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغُوا مِنْ أَشْغَالِهِمْ وَإِذَا بِغُبَارٍ قَدْطَارَ ثُمَّ مَحَقَ الْهَوَى ذَلِكَ الْغُبَارَ وَبَانَ مِنْ تَحْتِهِ عَسْكَرٌ جَرَّارٌ وَتَبَيَّنَ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ الْعَسْكَرَ عَسْكَرُ بَغْدَادَ وَخُرَاسَانَ وَمُقَدِّمُهُ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ وَكُلُّهُمْ فَرِحُونَ بِسَلْطَنَةِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghū min ashghālihim wa-idhā bi-ghubārin qadṭāra thumma maḥaqa al-hawā dhālika al-ghubāra wa-bāna min taḥtihi ʿaskarun jarrārun wa-tabayyana anna dhālika al-ʿaskara ʿaskaru baghdāda wa-khurāsāna wa-muqaddimuhu al-wazīru dandānu wa-kulluhum fariḥūna bi-salṭanati ḍawʾi al-makāni
sentences.l: And when they had finished with their tasks, then behold, a dust that had risen; then the air wiped away that dust, and from beneath it appeared a trailing army, and it became clear that that army was the army of Baghdad and Khurasan, its vanguard the vizier Dandān, and all of them rejoicing in the sultanate of Ḍawʾ al-Makān.
sentences.i: When they had finished their tasks, behold, a cloud of dust rose; then the wind swept that dust away, and from beneath it appeared a vast army, and it became clear that it was the army of Baghdad and Khurasan, led by the vizier Dandān, every man of them glad of the sultanate of Ḍawʾ al-Makān.
sentences.n: The print has قدطار as one word (قد + طار, “had flown up”). الهوى is “the air”.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ لَابِساً خِلْعَةَ الْمُلْكِ مُتَقَلِّداً بِسَيْفِ الْمَوْكِبِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna ḍawʾu al-makāni lābisan khilʿata al-mulki mutaqallidan bi-sayfi al-mawkibi
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān was wearing the robe of kingship, girded with the sword of the procession.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān was clothed in the robe of kingship and girded with the sword of state.

sentences.t: فَقَدَّمَ لَهُ الْحَاجِبُ الْفَرَسَ فَرَكِبَ وَسَارَ هُوَ وَمَمَالِيكُهُ وَجَمِيعُ مَنْ فِى الْخِيَامِ مُشَاةً فِي خِدْمَتِهِ حَتَّى دَخَلَ الْقُبَّةَ الْكَبِيرَةَ وَجَلَسَ
sentences.tr: fa-qaddama lahu al-ḥājibu al-farasa fa-rakiba wa-sāra huwa wa-mamālīkuhu wa-jamīʿu man fī al-khiyāmi mushātan fī khidmatihi ḥattā dakhala al-qubbata al-kabīrata wa-jalasa
sentences.l: So the chamberlain presented to him the horse, and he rode, and he went, he and his mamluks and all who were in the tents on foot in his service, until he entered the great dome and sat.
sentences.i: The chamberlain brought him the horse and he mounted and rode on, with his mamluks and everyone in the tents walking in his service, until he entered the great pavilion and sat down.

sentences.t: وَوَضَعَ النَّمْشَةَ عَلَى فَخِذَيْهِ وَوَقَفَ الْحَاجِبُ فِي خِدْمَتِهِ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَوَقَفَتْ مَمَالِيكُهُ فِي دِهْلِيزِ الْخَيْمَةِ وَشَهَرُوا فِي أَيْدِيهِمُ السُّيُوفَ
sentences.tr: wa-waḍaʿa al-namshata ʿalā fakhidhayhi wa-waqafa al-ḥājibu fī khidmatihi bayna yadayhi wa-waqafat mamālīkuhu fī dihlīzi al-khaymati wa-shaharū fī aydīhimu al-suyūfa
sentences.l: And he put the namsha upon his two thighs, and the chamberlain stood in his service between his hands, and his mamluks stood in the passage of the tent, and they drew in their hands the swords.
sentences.i: He laid the short sword across his thighs; the chamberlain stood before him in attendance, and his mamluks stood in the entrance passage of the tent with drawn swords in their hands.
sentences.n: النمشة is read as a kind of short sword (uncertain).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَتِ الْعَسَاكِرُ وَالْجُيُوشُ وَطَلَبُوا الْإِذْنَ فَدَخَلَ الْحَاجِبُ وَاسْتَأْذَنَ لَهُمُ السُّلْطَانَ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ فَأَمَرَأَنْ يَدْخُلُوا عَلَيْهِ عَشَرَةً عَشَرَةً فَأَعْلَمَهُمُ الْحَاجِبُ بِذَلِكَ فَأَجَابُوا بِالسَّمْعِ وَالطَّاعَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma aqbalati al-ʿasākiru wa-al-juyūshu wa-ṭalabū al-idhna fa-dakhala al-ḥājibu wa-istaʾdhana lahumu al-sulṭāna ḍawʾa al-makāni fa-amara an yadkhulū ʿalayhi ʿasharatan ʿasharatan fa-aʿlamahumu al-ḥājibu bi-dhālika fa-ajābū bi-al-samʿi wa-al-ṭāʿati
sentences.l: Then the troops and the armies came forward and asked for leave, and the chamberlain entered and asked leave for them of the sultan Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and he commanded that they enter upon him ten by ten, and the chamberlain informed them of that, and they answered with hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: Then the troops and armies came forward and asked for admission. The chamberlain went in and asked the sultan Ḍawʾ al-Makān's leave for them, and the sultan ordered that they come in to him ten at a time. The chamberlain told them so, and they answered with hearing and obedience.
sentences.n: The print runs أمر and أن together (فامران), read as two words.

sentences.t: وَوَقَفَ الْجَمِيعُ عَلَى بَابِ الدِّهْلِيزِ فَدَخَلَتْ عَشَرَةٌ مِنْهُمْ فَشَقَّ بِهِمُ الْحَاجِبُ فِى الدِّهْلِيزِ وَدَخَلَ بِهِمْ عَلَى السُّلْطَانِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ هَابُوهُ فَتَلَقَّاهُمْ أَحْسَنَ مُلْتَقًى
sentences.tr: wa-waqafa al-jamīʿu ʿalā bābi al-dihlīzi fa-dakhalat ʿasharatun minhum fa-shaqqa bihimu al-ḥājibu fī al-dihlīzi wa-dakhala bihim ʿalā al-sulṭāni ḍawʾi al-makāni fa-lammā raʾawhu hābūhu fa-talaqqāhum aḥsana multaqan
sentences.l: And all stood at the door of the passage, and ten of them entered, and the chamberlain cleaved a way with them in the passage and entered with them upon the sultan Ḍawʾ al-Makān; and when they saw him they stood in awe of him, and he met them with the best of meetings.
sentences.i: All of them waited at the door of the passage, and ten went in; the chamberlain led them through the passage and brought them before the sultan Ḍawʾ al-Makān. When they saw him they were awed, and he received them with the utmost graciousness.

sentences.t: وَوَعَدَهُمْ بِكُلِّ خَيْرٍ فَهَنَّوْهُ بِالسَّلَامَةِ وَدَعَوْالَهُ وَحَلَفُوالَهُ الْأَيْمَانَ الصَّادِقَةَ أَنَّهُمْ لَايُخَالِفُونَ لَهُ أَمْراً
sentences.tr: wa-waʿadahum bi-kulli khayrin fa-hannawhu bi-al-salāmati wa-daʿaw lahu wa-ḥalafū lahu al-aymāna al-ṣādiqata annahum lā yukhālifūna lahu amran
sentences.l: And he promised them every good, and they congratulated him upon his safety, and prayed for him, and swore to him the true oaths that they would not oppose him in any command.
sentences.i: He promised them every kindness; they congratulated him on his safe arrival, prayed for him, and swore to him the most solemn oaths that they would never go against any command of his.
sentences.n: The print joins ودعوا له, وحلفوا له and لا يخالفون as single words; they are read apart. “Congratulated him upon his safety” (هنّوه بالسلامة) is the usual greeting on a safe return; the edition prints هنوه without hamza.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَبَّلُوا الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَانْصَرَفُوا وَدَخَلَتْ عَشَرَةٌ أُخْرَى فَفَعَلَ بِهِمْ مِثْلَ مَافَعَلَ بِغَيْرِهِمْ
sentences.tr: thumma qabbalū al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-inṣarafū wa-dakhalat ʿasharatun ukhrā fa-faʿala bihim mithla mā faʿala bi-ghayrihim
sentences.l: Then they kissed the ground between his hands and departed, and another ten entered, and he did with them like what he had done with others.
sentences.i: Then they kissed the ground before him and withdrew, and another ten came in, and he did with them just as he had done with the others.
sentences.n: The print joins مثل ما فعل into مثل مافعل.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا يَدْخُلُونَ عَشَرَةً بَعْدَ عَشَرَةٍ حَتَّى لَمْ يَبْقَ غَيْرُ الْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ وَقَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَأَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazālū yadkhulūna ʿasharatan baʿda ʿasharatin ḥattā lam yabqa ghayru al-wazīri dandāna fa-dakhala ʿalayhi wa-qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhi fa-qāma ilayhi ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-aqbala ʿalayhi wa-qāla lahu
sentences.l: And they did not cease entering, ten after ten, until none remained but the vizier Dandān; and he entered upon him and kissed the ground between his hands, and Ḍawʾ al-Makān rose to him and turned to him and said to him:
sentences.i: They went on coming in, ten after ten, until no one was left but the vizier Dandān. He went in and kissed the ground before him, and Ḍawʾ al-Makān rose to meet him, turned to him, and said:
sentences.n: The print has بيق, a misprint for يبق, corrected here.

sentences.t: مَرْحَباً بِالْوَزِيرِ وَالْوَالِدِ الْكَبِيرَأَنَّ فِعْلَكَ فِعْلُ الْمُشِيرِ الْعَزِيزِ وَالتَّدْبِيرُ بِيَدِ اللَّطِيفِ الْخَبِيرِ
sentences.tr: marḥaban bi-al-wazīri wa-al-wālidi al-kabīra anna fiʿlaka fiʿlu al-mushīri al-ʿazīzi wa-al-tadbīru bi-yadi al-laṭīfi al-khabīri
sentences.l: Welcome to the vizier and the great father! Indeed your deed is the deed of the dear counsellor, and the ordering is in the hand of the Subtle, the All-Aware.
sentences.i: Welcome, vizier, great father! Truly what you have done is the deed of a dear counsellor — and the ordering of all things lies in the hand of the Subtle, the All-Aware.
sentences.n: Again the print runs the particle أن into the word before it (الكبيران). “The Subtle, the All-Aware” are two of God's names.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَ لِلْحَاجِبِ أَنِ اخْرُجْ فِي تِلْكَ السَّاعَةِ وَأَمَرَ بِمَدِّ السِّمَاطِ وَأَمَرَ بِإِحْضَارِ الْعَسْكَرِ جَمِيعاً فَحَضَرُوا وَأَكَلُو وَشَرِبُوا
sentences.tr: thumma amara li-al-ḥājibi ani ikhruj fī tilka al-sāʿati wa-amara bi-maddi al-simāṭi wa-amara bi-iḥḍāri al-ʿaskari jamīʿan fa-ḥaḍarū wa-akalū wa-sharibū
sentences.l: Then he commanded the chamberlain to go out at that hour, and commanded the spreading of the table, and commanded the bringing of the army, all of it, and they came, and ate, and drank.
sentences.i: Then he told the chamberlain to go out at once, ordered the banquet cloth to be spread, and summoned the whole army; they came, and ate and drank.
sentences.n: The print has واكلو without the final alif.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ قَالَ لِلْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ اِءْمُرِ الْعَسْكَرَ بِالْإِقَامَةِ عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ حَتَّى أَخْتَلِيَ بِكَ وَتُخْبِرَنِي بِسَبَبِ قَتْلِ أَبِي فَامْتَثَلَ الْوَزِيرُ قَوْلَ السُّلْطَانِ وَقَالَ لَابُدَّ مِنْ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika ḍawʾa al-makāni qāla li-al-wazīri dandāna iʾmuri al-ʿaskara bi-al-iqāmati ʿashrata ayyāmin ḥattā akhtaliyā bika wa-tukhbiranī bi-sababi qatli abī fa-imtathala al-wazīru qawla al-sulṭāni wa-qāla lā budda min dhālika
sentences.l: Then the king Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to the vizier Dandān: Command the army to stay ten days, until I be alone with you and you inform me of the cause of the killing of my father. And the vizier obeyed the word of the sultan and said: There is no escape from that.
sentences.i: Then King Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to the vizier Dandān: “Order the army to stay ten days, so that I may be alone with you and you may tell me why my father was killed.” The vizier obeyed the sultan and said, “It must be done.”
sentences.n: اءمر is the print's spelling of the imperative “command!”, with a separate hamza sign after the alif.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ خَرَجَ إِلَى وَسَطِ الْخِيَامِ وَأَمَرَا عَسْكَرَ بِالْإِقَامَةِ عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ فَامْتَثَلُوا أَمْرَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma kharaja ilā wasaṭi al-khiyāmi wa-amarā ʿaskara bi-al-iqāmati ʿashrata ayyāmin fa-imtathalū amrahu
sentences.l: Then he went out to the middle of the tents and commanded the army to stay ten days, and they obeyed his command.
sentences.i: Then he went out into the middle of the camp and ordered the army to stay ten days, and they obeyed.
sentences.n: The print has وامرا عسكر for وأمر العسكر, the alif of the article apparently displaced; read as “and he commanded the army”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَزِيرَ أَعْطَاهُمْ إِذْناً أَنَّهُمْ يَتَفَرَّجُونَ وَلَايَدْخُلُ أَحَدٌ مِنْ أَرْبَابِ الْخِدْمَةِ لِأَجْلِ الْخِدْمَةِ عِنْدَ الْمَلِكِ مُدَّةَ ثَلٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فَتَضَرَّعَ جَمِيعُ النَّاسِ وَدَعَوُا الضَّوْءَ الْمَكَانِ بِدَوَامِ الْعِزِّ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-wazīra aʿṭāhum idhnan annahum yatafarrajūna wa-lā yadkhulu aḥadun min arbābi al-khidmati li-ajli al-khidmati ʿinda al-maliki muddata thalāthati ayyāmin fa-taḍarraʿa jamīʿu al-nāsi wa-daʿawu al-ḍawʾa al-makāni bi-dawāmi al-ʿizzi
sentences.l: Then the vizier gave them leave to amuse themselves, and that none of the masters of service should enter, for the sake of service, upon the king for a period of three days; and all the people humbled themselves and prayed for the Ḍawʾ al-Makān for the permanence of glory.
sentences.i: Then the vizier gave them leave to amuse themselves, and ordered that none of the officers should come to wait on the king for three days. All the people raised their voices in thanks and prayed that Ḍawʾ al-Makān's glory might endure.
sentences.n: The print writes the king's name with the article (الضوء المكان); it is read as the same name. ثلثة is the defective spelling of ثلاثة, marked with a dagger alif. تضرّع is to “humble oneself”, here in thanks and supplication.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ الْوَزِيرُ وَأَعْلَمَهُ بِالَّذِي كَانَ فَصَبَرَ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ وَدَخَلَ عَلَى أُخْتِهِ نُزْهَةِ الزَّمَانِ وَقَالَ لَهَا
sentences.tr: thumma aqbala ʿalayhi al-wazīru wa-aʿlamahu bi-alladhī kāna fa-ṣabara ilā al-layli wa-dakhala ʿalā ukhtihi nuzhati al-zamāni wa-qāla lahā
sentences.l: Then the vizier turned to him and informed him of what had been; and he was patient until the night, and entered upon his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān and said to her:
sentences.i: Then the vizier turned to him and told him what had happened; he waited until night, then went in to his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān and said to her:
sentences.n: The king waits until night so that his sister can hear the account too; she listens from behind a curtain, as the next lines show.

sentences.t: أَهَلْ عَلِمْتِ بِسَبَبِ قَتْلِ أَبِي أَمْ لَمْ تَعْلَمِي بِسَبَبِهِ كَيْفَ كَانَ
sentences.tr: ahal ʿalimti bi-sababi qatli abī am lam taʿlamī bi-sababihi kayfa kāna
sentences.l: Did you know the cause of the killing of my father, or did you not know of its cause, how it was?
sentences.i: Did you know why our father was killed, or have you not learned the cause — how it came about?
sentences.n: أهل is a Middle Arabic blend of the question-particle أ and هل.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ لَمْ أَعْلَمْ سَبَبَ قَتْلِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu lam aʿlam sababa qatlihi
sentences.l: So she said to him: I did not know the cause of his killing.
sentences.i: She answered, “I do not know why he was killed.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا ضَرَبَتْ لَهَا سِتَارَةً مِنْ حَرِيرٍ وَجَلَسَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ خَارِجَ السِّتَارَةِ وَأَمَرَ بِإِحْضَارِ الْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ فَحَضَرَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā ḍarabat lahā sitāratan min ḥarīrin wa-jalasa ḍawʾu al-makāni khārija al-sitārati wa-amara bi-iḥḍāri al-wazīri dandāna fa-ḥaḍara bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: Then she struck for herself a curtain of silk, and Ḍawʾ al-Makān sat outside the curtain, and commanded the bringing of the vizier Dandān, and he came between his hands.
sentences.i: Then she had a silk curtain hung for herself, and Ḍawʾ al-Makān sat outside the curtain and sent for the vizier Dandān, who came and stood before him.
sentences.n: The print has السنارة, a misprint for الستارة, corrected here.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أُرِيدَأَنْ تُخْبِرَنِي تَفْصِيلاً بِسَبَبِ قَتْلِ أَبِي الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu urīda an tukhbiranī tafṣīlan bi-sababi qatli abī al-maliki ʿumara bni al-nuʿmāni
sentences.l: So he said to him: I want you to inform me in detail of the cause of the killing of my father the king ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān.
sentences.i: He said to him, “I want you to tell me in full why my father, King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, was killed.”
sentences.n: The print joins أريد أن into one word (اريدان).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ اِعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَّ الْمَلِكَ عُمَرَ بْنَ النُّعْمَانِ لَمَّا أَتَى مِنْ سَفَرِهِ مِنَ الصَّيْدِ وَالْقَنْصِ وَجَاءَ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ سَأَلَ عَنْكُمَا فَلَمْ يَجِدْكُمَا فَعَلِمَ أَنَّكُمَا قَدْ قَصَدْتُمَا الْحَجَّ فَاغْتَمَّ لِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru dandānu iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku anna al-malika ʿumara bna al-nuʿmāni lammā atā min safarihi mina al-ṣaydi wa-al-qanṣi wa-jāʾa ilā al-madīnati saʾala ʿankumā fa-lam yajidkumā fa-ʿalima annakumā qad qaṣadtumā al-ḥajja fa-ightamma li-dhālika
sentences.l: So the vizier Dandān said: Know, O king, that the king ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, when he came from his journey, from the hunting and the chase, and came to the city, asked about the two of you and did not find you, so he knew that you two had set out for the pilgrimage, and was grieved at that.
sentences.i: The vizier Dandān said: Know, O king, that when King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān returned from his journey of hunting and the chase and came to the city, he asked after the two of you and did not find you. He understood that you had set out on the pilgrimage, and was grieved by it.

sentences.t: فَازْدَادَ بِهِ الْغَيْظُ وَضَاقَ صَدْرُهُ وَأَقَامَ نِصْفَ سَنَةٍ وَهُوَ يَسْتَخْبِرُ عَنْكُمَا كُلَّ شَارِدٍ وَوَارِدٍ فَلَمْ يُخْبِرْهُ أَحَدٌ عَنْكُمَا
sentences.tr: fa-izdāda bihi al-ghayẓu wa-ḍāqa ṣadruhu wa-aqāma niṣfa sanatin wa-huwa yastakhbiru ʿankumā kulla shāridin wa-wāridin fa-lam yukhbirhu aḥadun ʿankumā
sentences.l: And rage increased in him, and his breast was straitened, and he stayed half a year, inquiring about you two of every straggler and every comer, and no one informed him about you.
sentences.i: His anger grew, and he felt hemmed in; he waited half a year, asking every wanderer and every arrival about you, and no one could tell him anything.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا نَحْنُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ يَوْماً مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ بَعْدَ مَا مَضَى لَكُمَا سَنَةٌ كَامِلَةٌ مِنْ تَارِيخِ فَقْدِكُمَا وَإِذَا بِعَجُوزٍ عَلَيْهَا آثَارُ الْعِبَادَةِ قَدْ وَرَدَتْ عَلَيْنَا وَمَعَهَا خَمْسُ جَوَارٍ نُهَّدٌ أَبْكَارٌ كَأَنَّهُنَّ الْأَقْمَارُ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā naḥnu bayna yadayhi yawman mina al-ayyāmi baʿda mā maḍā lakumā sanatun kāmilatun min tārīkhi faqdikumā wa-idhā bi-ʿajūzin ʿalayhā āthāru al-ʿibādati qad waradat ʿalaynā wa-maʿahā khamsu jawārin nuhhadun abkārun ka-annahunna al-aqmāru
sentences.l: And while we were between his hands one day of the days, after a whole year had passed for you two from the date of your loss, and behold, an old woman, upon her the marks of worship, had come to us, and with her five girls, high-breasted virgins, as if they were the moons,
sentences.i: One day, while we were in attendance on him, a full year after the date of your disappearance, an old woman came in — a woman with the marks of devotion upon her — and with her five young girls, full-breasted virgins, like moons,
sentences.n: “As if they were the moons”: كأنهن with كـ, “like”, + أنّ + the attached pronoun, a comparison.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ حَوَيْنَ مِنَ الْحُسْنِ وَالْجَمَالِ مَا يَعْجِزُ عَنْ وَصْفِهِ اللِّسَانُ
sentences.tr: wa-qad ḥawayna mina al-ḥusni wa-al-jamāli mā yaʿjizu ʿan waṣfihi al-lisānu
sentences.l: and they had gathered of beauty and loveliness what the tongue is unable to describe.
sentences.i: possessed of a beauty and loveliness that no tongue could describe.

sentences.t: وَمَعَ كَمَالِ حُسْنِهِنَّ يَقْرَأْنَ الْقُرْآنَ وَيَعْرِفْنَ الْحِكْمَةَ وَأَخْبَارَ الْمُتَقَدِّمِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-maʿa kamāli ḥusnihinna yaqraʾna al-qurʾāna wa-yaʿrifna al-ḥikmata wa-akhbāra al-mutaqaddimīna
sentences.l: And together with the perfection of their beauty they recite the Qurʾān and know wisdom and the reports of the ancients.
sentences.i: And with all their perfect beauty, they recited the Qurʾān and knew wisdom and the chronicles of the ancients.

sentences.t: فَاسْتَأْذَنَتْ تِلْكَ الْعَجُوزُ فِي الدُّخُولِ عَلَى الْمَلِكِ فَأَذِنَ لَهَا فَدَخَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَقَبَّلَتِ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-istaʾdhanat tilka al-ʿajūzu fī al-dukhūli ʿalā al-maliki fa-adhina lahā fa-dakhalat ʿalayhi wa-qabbalati al-arḍa bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: So that old woman asked leave to enter upon the king, and he gave her leave, and she entered upon him and kissed the ground between his hands.
sentences.i: The old woman asked leave to come in to the king; he allowed it, and she went in and kissed the ground before him.

sentences.t: وَكُنْتُ أَنَا جَالِساً بِجَانِبِ الْمَلِكِ فَلَمَّا دَخَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ قَرَّبَهَا اللهُ لِمَا رَأَى عَلَيْهَا مِنْ آثَارِ الزُّهْدِ وَالْعِبَادَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-kuntu anā jālisan bi-jānibi al-maliki fa-lammā dakhalat ʿalayhi qarrabahā allāhu li-mā raʾā ʿalayhā min āthāri al-zuhdi wa-al-ʿibādati
sentences.l: And I was sitting at the side of the king, and when she entered upon him, God brought her near, because of what he saw upon her of the marks of asceticism and worship.
sentences.i: I was sitting beside the king. When she came in, he drew her close, seeing in her the marks of asceticism and devotion.
sentences.n: The print has قربها الله, “God brought her near”; the sense is that the king drew her near, and الله may be a slip for الملك.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا اسْتَقَرَّتِ الْعَجُوزُ عِنْدَهُ أَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā istaqarrati al-ʿajūzu ʿindahu aqbalat ʿalayhi wa-qālat lahu
sentences.l: And when the old woman was settled with him, she turned to him and said to him:
sentences.i: When the old woman had settled before him, she turned to him and said:

sentences.t: اِعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَّ مَعِي خَمْسَ جَوَارٍ مَا مَلَكَ أَحَدٌ مِنَ الْمُلُوكِ مِثْلَهُنَّ لِأَنَّهُنَّ ذَوَاتُ عَقْلٍ وَجَمَالٍ وَحُسْنٍ وَكَمَالٍ يَقْرَأْنَ الْقُرْآنَ بِالرِّوَايَاتِ وَيَعْرِفْنَ الْعُلُومَ وَأَخْبَارَ الْأُمَمِ السَّالِفَةِ
sentences.tr: iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku anna maʿī khamsa jawārin mā malaka aḥadun mina al-mulūki mithlahunna li-annahunna dhawātu ʿaqlin wa-jamālin wa-ḥusnin wa-kamālin yaqraʾna al-qurʾāna bi-al-riwāyāti wa-yaʿrifna al-ʿulūma wa-akhbāra al-umami al-sālifati
sentences.l: Know, O king, that with me are five girls the like of whom none of the kings has owned, because they are possessors of intellect and loveliness and beauty and perfection; they recite the Qurʾān in the transmissions, and know the sciences and the reports of the nations of old.
sentences.i: Know, O king, that I have with me five girls the like of whom no king has ever owned, for they are women of intellect, loveliness, beauty and perfection. They recite the Qurʾān in its various transmissions, and they know the sciences and the chronicles of nations long past.
sentences.n: “In the transmissions” (بالروايات) are the canonical variant readings of the Qurʾān.

sentences.t: وَهُنَّ بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ وَاقِفَاتٌ فِي خِدْمَتِكَ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ وَعِنْدَ الِامْتِحَانِ يُكْرَمُ الْمَرْءُ أَوْيُهَانُ
sentences.tr: wa-hunna bayna yadayka wāqifātun fī khidmatika yā malika al-zamāni wa-ʿinda al-imtiḥāni yukramu al-marʾu aw yuhānu
sentences.l: And they are between your hands, standing in your service, O king of the age; and at the testing a man is honoured or disgraced.
sentences.i: They stand before you now, in your service, O king of the age — and when a person is put to the test, he is honoured or disgraced.
sentences.n: The closing saying is proverbial: “at the test a man is honoured or disgraced”. The print joins أو and يهان.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ الْمَرْحُومُ وَالِدُكَ إِلَى الْجَوَارِي فَسَرَّتْهُ رُؤْيَتُهُنَّ وَقَالَ لَهُنَّ كُلُّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْكُنَّ تُسْمِعُنِي شَيْأً تَعْرِفُهُ مِنْ أَخْبَارِ النَّاسِ الْمَاضِينَ وَالْأُمَمِ السَّابِقِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara al-marḥūmu wālidaka ilā al-jawārī fa-sarrathu ruʾyatuhunna wa-qāla lahunna kullu wāḥidatin minkunna tusmiʿunī shayʾan taʿrifuhu min akhbāri al-nāsi al-māḍīna wa-al-umami al-sābiqīna
sentences.l: So the late-lamented, your father, looked at the girls, and the sight of them delighted him, and he said to them: Each one of you shall let me hear something that she knows of the reports of the people who have passed and the nations that went before.
sentences.i: Your late father looked at the girls and was delighted by the sight of them. He said to them, “Each of you must let me hear something she knows of the stories of people who have passed away, and of the nations of old.”
sentences.n: المرحوم, “the one to whom mercy has been shown”, is the courteous way of speaking of the dead. تسمعني is a present tense used as a command (“let me hear”).

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahra zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Then morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted tale unsaid.
